entries.name: MiniUp
entries.description: MiniUp — turn HTML into a hosted micro-app/site: create, upload assets, and publish/unpublish to a live URL.

usage.callShape: POST https://www.miniup.io/api/x402/apps with JSON body {name, html, visibility?, password?}
quirks: The 'name' field is a globally-unique slug. A taken or invalid slug returns HTTP 400 'Page name unavailable' AND STILL CHARGES $0.007. Use a unique random slug.
required fields: name + html; html must be a complete HTML document used as index.html.
Response gives app.status='created', no explicit live URL field; the URL is derived from the slug.
visibility:'public'|'private'; supplying 'password' makes the app private.
usage.guide: Create a hosted micro-app by POSTing JSON {name, html} to https://www.miniup.io/api/x402/apps (x402, ~$0.007 USDC on Base, no API key). 'name' is a globally-unique slug — generate a random one, because a taken/invalid slug returns 400 'Page name unavailable' yet still charges you. 'html' is the full HTML document served as index.html; add visibility:'public'|'private' (or a password for private). On success (200) read body.app.appId and body.app.status='created'; the on-chain receipt is at body.receipt.txHash. The response gives no explicit live URL — it is derived from the slug.

entries.name: Render
entries.description: Access the Render PaaS API (deploy/manage web services, static sites, cron jobs, databases) metered per call via an x402 pay-per-call gateway (HTTPay) at $0.001/call — no Render account or API key required.

usage.callShape: POST https://httpay.xyz/api/gateway/render/v1/services with JSON body (x402 payment, $0.001) — but additionally requires an upstream Render API key via X-Upstream-Token header
usage.outputShape: body.error / body.instructions (401 auth-required error; no usable result without upstream key)
quirks: x402 payment settles ($0.001 charged on Base) BEFORE the auth check — you pay even though the call fails with 401.
Despite the registry description claiming 'no Render account or API key required', the HTTPay gateway requires the caller's OWN upstream Render bearer token passed via the X-Upstream-Token header.
Response 401 body lists accepted authFormats (bearer/token/bot/basic/apikey). Without a real upstream Render API key the endpoint cannot return any data.
This is the known HTTPay charge-then-401 gateway pattern for services that proxy a key-gated upstream API — it violates the no-API-key registry policy and should be pruned.
usage.guide: This endpoint is BROKEN for keyless agent use. Calling POST https://httpay.xyz/api/gateway/render/v1/services pays $0.001 USDC via x402 but then returns HTTP 401 'Service render requires authentication' demanding an upstream Render API key via the X-Upstream-Token header. There is no way to get a useful result without supplying your own Render bearer token, which contradicts the registry's no-API-key requirement. Do not call it expecting Render data; it should be dropped from the keyless registry.

entries.name: Host Website (ZeroClick)
entries.description: ZeroClick — host a website and get a live URL.

usage.callShape: GET https://site.withzero.ai/run (x402) — UNREACHABLE, host does not respond
usage.outputShape: none — no response received (connection times out)
quirks: Host site.withzero.ai resolves to Cloudflare IPs (104.21.6.9, 172.67.134.34) but the origin never completes a TCP/TLS connection — every request hangs and returns HTTP 000 after timeout.
The apex withzero.ai also times out (HTTP 000), indicating the whole site/origin is down, not just the /run route.
Control check passed: https://www.google.com returned HTTP 200 from the same environment, confirming egress works — the failure is the target host, not the network.
No 402 / payment requirements were ever returned, so price ('Varies') and payment.accepts (empty) could not be confirmed.
qa-pay returned classification 'wallet-error' with 'provider request failed: fetch failed' — this is the upstream fetch failing, NOT a wallet/balance problem; nothing was charged.
usage.guide: This endpoint is currently broken/unreachable. GET https://site.withzero.ai/run never responds — DNS resolves to Cloudflare but the origin times out on every connection, and the apex withzero.ai is also down. Do not attempt to pay; no 402 quote is returned and no work can be done. Re-test later to see if the host comes back online; if it does, the documented call shape (bare GET /run, x402-gated, intended to host a website and return a live URL) will need fresh discovery since the input/output schema was never observable.
